content.text: MC acute form of leukemia in adults
Median onset 65yrs; 20% of cases of childhood leukemia
•t(15; 17) associated w/ DIC, Auer rods, & myeloperoxidase activity
•associated w/ infiltration of the gums (gingival hyperplasia)
25% of children develop bone pain or arthralgia d/t leukemic infiltration of perichondral bone or leukemic expansion of marrow cavity
May develop soft-tissue tumor called chloroma in spinal cord or skin; greenish hue
Progressive bone marrow failure leads to pallor, ecchymoses or petechiae, & fever
Bone marrow examination FNA & bx – confirmatory
↑ K, ↓ Ca, ↑ phos, hyperuricemia, renal failure
: fusion of 2 genes: BCR (chromosome 22) & ABL1 (chromosome 9), resulting in the BCR-ABL1 fusion gene.
(abnormal chromosome 22 which harbors the BCR-ABL1 gene)
Fatigue, night sweats, malaise, weight loss, fever
•malignancy arising from immature lymphoid stem cells in the bone marrow
•B cell (MC!), T cell, or null type (non B or T cell)
: overpopulation of immature WBCs (blasts) overtake normal hematopoiesis resulting in pancytopenia
CHILD + LAD + BONE PAIN + bleeding + fever
•precursor T cell MC associated w/ adolescents w/ mediastinal mass & CNS sxs
: kills detectable disease for complete remission
: short term intensive therapy to sustain remission
: low dose to eradicate any remaining undetectable cells
